title: Coefficient compatibility of the normalized proper/open interchange
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be any of the coefficient maps specified in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]: a homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for finite $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $\mathcal O_E\to E$, $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a continuous map $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite admissible ring, or a finite composite. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring; use pulled-back condensed coefficients, including the finite-subextension condensed convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Work in ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories on the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $T_V=\Lambda'_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_V}-$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], $\gamma_{v,M}:T Rv_*M\to Rv_*TM$ for the unit/pullback/counit comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image], and $\delta_{a,M}:T a_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!TM$ for the canonical open comparison [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso, det-prop-scalar-six-pullback]. The notation $\Dctf$ means bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper and $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ a quasi-compact open immersion. Choose a dense compactification $\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow r\overline Y$ of $ip$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Use $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$, $r|_{\overline X}=p$, and the natural map $\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ characterized by restriction to $\operatorname{id}_{Rp_*A}$, as in [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange]. For every $A\in\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$ the coefficient square is
$$Rr_*\delta_{j',A}\circ\gamma_{r,j'_!A}\circ T_{\overline Y}(\iota_A)
=\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}\circ i_!\gamma_{p,A}\circ\delta_{i,Rp_*A}.$$
Its source is $T_{\overline Y}i_!Rp_*A$ and its target is $Rr_*j'_!T_{\overline X}A$. Under the canonical open-restriction and pullback/coefficient identifications, the restriction of each side to $Y$ is $\gamma_{p,A}$. The source and target are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude over $\Lambda'$.

proof.text: Use [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] (1) to identify $W\times_{\overline Y}Y$ with $\overline X$, with projections $j'$ and $p$. For $R=\Lambda,\Lambda'$ write $u_{a,R}:1\xrightarrow{\sim}a_R^*a_{!,R}$ for the actual open unit. The open-restriction lemma gives $\rho_{R,B}:i_R^*Rr_{*,R}B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,R}j_R'^*B$ and the open adjunctions on the entire unbounded categories. Put $N=Rp_{*,\Lambda}A$, $B=j'_{!,\Lambda}A$, and $H_R(M)=Rr_{*,R}j'_{!,R}M$. Define $\sigma_{R,M}=Rp_{*,R}(u_{j',R,M}^{-1})\circ\rho_{R,j'_{!,R}M}$. The defining normalization of $\iota_M$ is precisely $\sigma_{R,M}\circ i_R^*(\iota_M)\circ u_{i,R,Rp_{*,R}M}=1$.

source.place: Composition, normalized Cartesian open square and interchange

proof.text: The $\rho_{R,B}$ just used is the actual unit--square--counit exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_{R,B}$ for this Cartesian square. Indeed, transpose its defining Hom chain under $p_R^*\dashv Rp_{*,R}$. The adjunct formula for $\beta^{-1}:j'_!p^*\to r^*i_!$ in [lem-sfb-condensed-open-square-scalar-comparison] is $\theta\circ p^*u_i$. Substituting it in that chain and cancelling the open unit against its counit gives $j'^*(\varepsilon_{r,B})\circ\theta_{Rr_*B}$, the transpose defining $\operatorname{Ex}_{R,B}$ in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Equality follows from the adjunction bijection. The formula remains this formula on unbounded complexes: the cited open-square lemma localizes $\beta$ termwise, and the derived restriction lemma gives the same Hom chain there. Thus the exchange rectangle applies to the specified $\rho$, not an arbitrary isomorphism with these endpoints.

source.place: Composition, identification of canonical open restriction with its adjunction mate

proof.text:
Write $c_a:a_{\Lambda'}^*T\xrightarrow{\sim}Ta_\Lambda^*$ for the inverse pullback comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]. It is the inverse of the canonical comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), whose forward map is the scalar-adjunction mate of the restriction/inverse-image comparison [def-sfb-scalar-six-coefficient-interfaces]. By [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] this mate is $\theta_a$ and its inverse is the balanced K-flat comparison. Hence $c_a=\lambda_a=\theta_a^{-1}$ for the $\lambda$ of the rectangle and the $\theta$ of the open normalization below. The normalized exchange rectangle for $(r,p,i,j')$ and $B$ says
$$Rp_{*,\Lambda'}(c_{j',B})\rho_{\Lambda',T_WB}i_{\Lambda'}^*(\gamma_{r,B})=\gamma_{p,j_\Lambda'^*B}\,T_Y(\rho_{\Lambda,B})\,c_{i,Rr_{*,\Lambda}B}.$$
Its $\rho$ and $\gamma$ are those in steps 1--2: the rectangle defines $\gamma$ by exactly the same counit transpose as the direct-image node. The open scalar normalization gives, for $a=i,j'$,
$$u_{a,\Lambda',T M}^{-1}a_{\Lambda'}^*(\delta_{a,M})=T(u_{a,\Lambda,M}^{-1})c_{a,a_{!,\Lambda}M}.$$
These formulas apply to $M=A$ and $M=N$ without assuming either scalar map flat.

source.place: Composition, coefficient compatibility of the open-restriction exchange

proof.text:
Put $q=Rr_{*,\Lambda'}(\delta_{j',A})\circ\gamma_{r,B}$, and let $L=q\circ T_{\overline Y}(\iota_A)$ and $R=\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}\circ i_{!,\Lambda'}(\gamma_{p,A})\circ\delta_{i,N}$. Use the source identification $s=u_{i,\Lambda',T_YN}^{-1}\circ i_{\Lambda'}^*(\delta_{i,N})$ and target identification $t=\sigma_{\Lambda',T_{\overline X}A}$. Naturality of $\rho$ and $\gamma$, step 3 for $j'$, and the rectangle give
$$t\,i_{\Lambda'}^*q=\gamma_{p,A}\,T_Y(\sigma_{\Lambda,A})\,c_{i,H_\Lambda(A)}.$$
Now naturality of $c_i$, step 1's normalization, and step 3 for $i$ yield
$$t\,i_{\Lambda'}^*L=\gamma_{p,A}\,T_Y(u_{i,\Lambda,N}^{-1})c_{i,i_{!,\Lambda}N}=\gamma_{p,A}s.$$
For $R$, step 1 over $\Lambda'$ and naturality of the open unit give directly $t\,i_{\Lambda'}^*R=\gamma_{p,A}s$. Thus both restrictions are the specified $\gamma_{p,A}$ under the canonical identifications.

source.place: Composition, explicit calculation of both restrictions

proof.text: Precompose both maps by $\delta_{i,N}^{-1}$, so their common source becomes $i_{!,\Lambda'}T_YN$. Under $i_{!,\Lambda'}\dashv i_{\Lambda'}^*$, a map $f$ from this source has adjunct $i_{\Lambda'}^*(f)\circ u_{i,\Lambda',T_YN}$. The adjuncts of $L\delta_{i,N}^{-1}$ and $R\delta_{i,N}^{-1}$ agree by step 4. Injectivity of this adjunction bijection gives their equality, and cancellation of $\delta_{i,N}^{-1}$ gives $L=R$, the asserted square. This only uses the adjunction; no assertion that restriction is faithful on arbitrary objects is needed.

source.place: Composition, uniqueness by the open adjunction

proof.text: The hypotheses for constructibility hold: $p,r$ are proper maps of standing schemes and $i,j'$ are quasi-compact open immersions (the latter is part of a compactification). By [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images] (2)--(3), $Rp_*A$ and $i_!Rp_*A$ belong to $\Dctf$ over $\Lambda$. By [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf] (3), $T_{\overline Y}i_!Rp_*A$ belongs to $\Dctf(\overline Y,\Lambda')$ and $T_{\overline X}A$ belongs to $\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda')$. Apply the same direct-image stability clauses over $\Lambda'$ first to $j'_!$ and then to $Rr_*$ to get $Rr_*j'_!T_{\overline X}A\in\Dctf(\overline Y,\Lambda')$. This proves the final boundedness, constructibility and finite-Tor-amplitude assertion.
